record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.context_brief: Algorithms for pretty good state transfer
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with adjacency matrix A. Pretty good state transfer between vertices u and v means that there exists a sequence of times t_j for which |exp(i t_j A)_{uv}| tends to 1. Find a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether pretty good state transfer occurs in a given graph, and also give an algorithm that computes a subsequence of times witnessing that convergence.

evidence.quote: there could be distinct values of t for which the sequence (|exp(it_j A)_{uv}|)_{j\ge 0} converges to 1. When this occurs, we say that pretty good state transfer happens in G between u and v.
Find a polynomial time algorithm to test whether pretty good state transfer occurs, and find an algorithm to compute a subsequence of times which represent pretty good state transfer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and adjacency matrix $A \in \{0,1\}^{V\times V}$. For real $t$, consider the unitary $U(t) = \exp(i t A)$. Given two vertices $u, v \in V(G)$, we say that pretty good state transfer (PGST) occurs between $u$ and $v$ in $G$ if there exists a sequence of real times $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ such that
$$\lim_{j \to \infty} \bigl| \bigl(\exp(i t_j A)\bigr)_{uv} \bigr| = 1.$$

Solve the following two algorithmic problems:

(a) Design an algorithm that, given $G$ and a pair of vertices $u, v$, decides in time polynomial in $|V(G)|$ whether pretty good state transfer occurs between $u$ and $v$ in $G$.

(b) Design an algorithm that, whenever pretty good state transfer does occur between $u$ and $v$ in $G$, computes (in a constructive sense) an explicit sequence of times $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ witnessing the convergence $|(\exp(i t_j A))_{uv}| \to 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: While perfect state transfer can be decided in polynomial time on classical computers, deciding pretty good state transfer is more subtle: existing characterizations rely on Kronecker's theorem on simultaneous Diophantine approximation, for which no fully algorithmic (polynomial-time) version is known in this context. No general polynomial-time decision algorithm or general algorithm constructing the witnessing sequence of times appears in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Perfect state transfer is poly-time
status_evidence.snippet: Deciding whether a graph admits perfect state transfer can be done in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: Perfect state transfer (the stronger property) is known to be decidable in polynomial time, but no analogous result is established for pretty good state transfer.

status_evidence.title: Designing pretty good state transfer via isospectral reductions
status_evidence.snippet: The best known tool to decide existence of pretty good state transfer relies on Kronecker's theorem, for which an algorithmic version has not yet been found.
status_evidence.claim: General decidability of PGST currently depends on Kronecker-type number-theoretic conditions without a known polynomial-time algorithm.
